decisions.reason: Changing the number of tickets issued for a no-referral mint does not alter the independently specified commission allocation. The same message's $12 commission decision is already represented separately.
The source Event changes ticket issuance only for no-referral mints; coded-referral ticket issuance remains independently set to four tickets.
The no-referral ticket-count change does not modify coded-referral commissions. The same message's coded-referral commission decision is already represented separately.
A same-message MODIFY already revises the FAQ state to say that a no-code mint provides six tickets, so no additional or incomplete propagated Event remains.
Changing the reward quantity after a referral is absent or rejected does not change which referral identifiers are valid or the prohibition on self-referrals.
The number of no-referral tickets does not alter the NFT token serial used as the permanent referral identity or its display locations.
The ticket quantity created by a no-referral mint does not change the rule that active tickets follow the NFT upon transfer.
The current landing-page state describes coded-referral marketing and general prize mechanics, not the number of tickets assigned by a no-referral mint.
The current About-page state does not specify a no-referral ticket quantity, so changing that quantity from one to six leaves its represented content requirements unchanged.
Increasing tickets issued for a no-referral mint does not change the Small Block winner count, prize amount, draw trigger, eligibility method, or pool allocation.

The metadata requirement continues to require accurate ticket and reward data but does not store a separate no-referral ticket quantity. The same source reports a runtime metadata failure rather than changing this requirement's value.
The number of tickets created at mint time does not change their Small Block eligibility window, post-draw reset, or carry-forward behavior.
